content_of_post_to_comment:
So I finally saved up the money to purchase some e-bikes for me and my daughter and I must say we get out a lot more than ever! I am spending far less time online and more offline.

Lots of things have apparently changed. I kinda knew this already, because of my work. But when I am working its kinda like autopilot after so long. Trying to mingle with the locals in real life has taught me some new things:

Politics are now a no-no, you can NOT talk about politics, ever!

If you don't smile as kids walk by, you are a psychopath, if you do, you're a child molester. If you are wearing sunglasses-- because the parents can't see your eyes and assume you are trying to look up their kids' whatevers??? I guess???? When did this weird negative consensus happen and why? It is kinda offensive ngl..

If it is not summer...If a person walks by, it is a rare event. And almost never someone your age. Where did THEY all go?

Strangers talking to strangers is a big no-no, especially if you are of different origins. If you approach a stranger, be ready to be pepper-sprayed even if you are carrying a big sign that says "I am definitely not a criminal"

As for me, being a nearly-normal average looking citizen can ride around town and not be bothered by law enforcement. But it really bothers me to see any person hailing from the minority walking in/thru/around town get immediately questioned and half the time (yes half, I shit you not) of the time arrested by authorities of some sort. So bad that now minorities and people from other countries when in my town wear these panty-hose things over their heads+sunglasses. I think they have a name but can't remember what those are called off hand.

2 decades ago around here people left their doors unlocked and whatnot. Now most doors have at least 4 or more locks on them. Many of our windowed homes feature bars. Its sad. More often than not, people will switch sides if another person is coming up the road from the opposite direction on the same sidewalk, UNLESS they are dressed exactly like them or are a "Beautiful Person(TM)" which around here means white shirt, blue jeans, brand new accessories, shoes that are no more than 2 weeks old, and wearing enough perfume/cologne to knock out an elephant with a head cold.

I found that it wasn't that we don't have homeless people in our town, or that life is so good people actually are not homeless: it is that they moved out of town. They now live under an abandoned bridge down an abandoned section of highway (to take advantage of the camping on abandoned highway loophole thing). There's huge masses gathered at these safe spots. They tore down the homeless shelter here in town and built an extra police kiosk there for holding prisoners to be transferred to state prison. I am told many of the people who get sent there are homeless. Coincidence?

On the same topic: I also noticed after that, that at least 30% of the houses in my town are for sale, for rent, for lease, for rent-to-own, etc. The same can be said for industrial and office properties. Are we great again yet? Wasn't that supposed to be "soon".

Gas prices...wow I am so glad my summer vehicles are electric right now. I can go about 40-50 miles on my battery. And there is no reason to go more than 10. This area is a never-ending suburb dotted with the occasional metro area that stretches for hundreds of miles in every direction. You need to go at least 1000 miles west of here to get to anything that is not. 1000 miles east...would be the atlantic ocean. I miss the rocky mountains and the west coast now more than ever.
comment: The e-bike part actually caught my attention because getting people back outside seems to expose how much social habits have changed. I’ve noticed the same thing walking around neighborhoods: fewer casual conversations, more suspicion of strangers. Some of it is real safety concerns, but I wonder how much of it comes from years of people living through screens instead of shared spaces.
